content.text: 🤿 Be able to
🔁 Review

In our previous lesson, we explored modal verbs and their various functions in expressing ability, possibility, permission, obligation, and more. We examined how modals like can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would, and must are used in different contexts.
Quick Practice:
Identify the function of the modal verb in this sentence: "You must submit your application by Friday."
Rewrite this sentence using an appropriate modal verb: "It's possible that she will join us later."
What's the difference between "must" and "have to" when expressing obligation?
🎯 Overview

"Be able to" is a versatile alternative to the modal verbs "can" and "could" for expressing ability. Unlike modal verbs, which have limited forms, "be able to" can be used in all tenses, aspects, and with other modal verbs, making it an essential structure for expressing ability across different time frames.

The basic structure is formed with the appropriate form of "be" (am/is/are/was/were/will be/have been, etc.) followed by "able to" and the base form of the main verb. For example, "She is able to speak three languages" or "They will be able to attend the conference."

We use "be able to" when we need to express ability in tenses or constructions where "can" and "could" cannot be used, such as future, perfect, or continuous forms. It's also used to emphasize successful completion of a difficult action, especially in the past tense ("was/were able to").
🏊 Can you do?
Complete the sentences with the appropriate form of "be able to":

a. After taking the course, I _______ speak Spanish much more fluently. b. By next year, they _______ complete the construction project. c. She _______ solve the complex problem yesterday, which impressed everyone. d. We haven't _______ reach him by phone since he moved abroad.
Choose the correct option to complete each sentence:
a. I won't _______ attend the meeting tomorrow. i. can ii. be able to iii. could
b. She _______ play the piano since she was five years old. i. is able to ii. has been able to iii. can to
c. Despite the difficulties, they _______ finish the project on time last month. i. could ii. were able to iii. can
Rewrite these sentences using "be able to" in the appropriate form:
a. I can speak three languages. (future perfect) b. She could solve the problem. (present perfect) c. They can't attend the conference. (past simple) d. We can finish this today. (future continuous)
Identify whether "be able to" or a modal verb (can/could) would be more appropriate in these contexts:

a. I _______ swim since I was a child. (general ability in the present) b. After months of practice, she finally _______ play the entire sonata. (achievement in the past) c. _______ you help me with this heavy box? (request for help now) d. They _______ visit us next summer if their visa application is approved. (future possibility)
🔍 Deep Dive

"Be able to" is a crucial structure in English that allows us to express ability with greater flexibility than the modal verbs "can" and "could." Let's explore its various uses, forms, and nuances in detail.
Forms of "Be able to" Across Tenses
Present Simple
I am able to speak French. (I can speak French.)
She is able to solve complex problems. (She can solve complex problems.)
They are able to run five miles without stopping. (They can run five miles without stopping.)
Past Simple
I was able to finish the project on time. (I managed to finish the project on time.)
She was able to convince the committee. (She succeeded in convincing the committee.)
They were able to escape the burning building. (They managed to escape the burning building.)
Future Simple
I will be able to attend the conference next month.
She will be able to drive after she gets her license.
They will be able to afford a house once they save enough for a down payment.
Present Perfect
I have been able to improve my English significantly since I started taking classes.
She has been able to maintain a healthy work-life balance despite her busy schedule.
They have been able to increase productivity by implementing new technologies.
Past Perfect
I had been able to complete most of the work before the power outage.
She had been able to secure funding before the deadline.
They had been able to resolve the issues before the client noticed.
Future Perfect
By next year, I will have been able to save enough for a down payment.
She will have been able to publish her research by the time she graduates.
They will have been able to expand to three new markets by the end of the fiscal year.
Present Continuous
I am being able to focus better since I started meditating. (uncommon but possible in specific contexts)
She is being able to handle the pressure more effectively with her new coping strategies. (uncommon)
Present Perfect Continuous
I have been being able to sleep better since I started exercising regularly. (very uncommon)
With Modal Verbs
I might be able to help you tomorrow.
She should be able to complete the task by Friday.
They would be able to participate if they had more notice.
You must be able to swim to join the water sports club.
"Be able to" vs. "Can/Could"
While "be able to" and "can/could" both express ability, they are not always interchangeable. Here are the key differences:
Tense Flexibility
"Can" is limited to present and "could" to past or conditional situations.
"Be able to" can be used in all tenses and with other modal verbs.
Examples:
Present: I can swim. / I am able to swim. (interchangeable)
Past: I could swim when I was younger. / I was able to swim when I was younger. (generally interchangeable)
Future: I will be able to swim after I take lessons. (no equivalent with "can")
Perfect: I have been able to swim since I was a child. (no equivalent with "can")
Achievement vs. General Ability
In the past tense, "was/were able to" often emphasizes successful completion of a specific action, while "could" typically refers to a general ability.
Examples:
Despite the storm, we were able to reach the shore safely. (specific achievement)
When I was younger, I could run for hours without getting tired. (general ability)
Negative Forms
In negative forms, both structures express inability, but with subtle differences:
I can't speak Japanese. (general inability)
I am not able to speak Japanese. (perhaps more emphatic or formal)
I couldn't attend the meeting yesterday. (general statement about past inability)
I wasn't able to attend the meeting yesterday. (perhaps emphasizing the specific circumstance)
Special Uses of "Be able to"
Expressing Achievement
"Was/were able to" often emphasizes success in difficult circumstances:
Despite the challenges, she was able to complete the marathon.
They were able to escape the burning building just in time.
Formal or Professional Contexts
"Be able to" is often preferred in formal or professional settings:
Candidates must be able to work under pressure.
The successful applicant will be able to demonstrate excellent communication skills.
Future Abilities
Since "can" has no future form, "will be able to" is essential for discussing future abilities:
After the surgery, you will be able to walk without pain.
Once you complete the course, you will be able to apply for certification.
Hypothetical Situations
"Would be able to" is used for hypothetical or conditional abilities:
If I had more time, I would be able to help you.
She would be able to perform better with proper training.
Perfect Tenses
"Have/has/had been able to" expresses ability over a period of time:
I have been able to maintain my weight since I changed my diet.
They had been able to keep the secret until the surprise party.
Common Phrases and Collocations with "Be able to"
With Adverbs of Degree
She is barely able to keep up with the workload.
They are fully able to handle the responsibility.
I am hardly able to understand his accent.
With Time Expressions
I will eventually be able to speak fluently.
She has always been able to solve complex problems.
They have never been able to agree on this issue.
In Reported Speech
He said he would be able to attend the meeting.
She told me she had been able to secure funding.
They reported that they might not be able to meet the deadline.
Mini Dialogues:
Situation: Job Interview
Interviewer: Can you describe a challenging situation you've faced at work?
Candidate: Last year, our team was facing a tight deadline for a major project. Despite limited resources, I was able to reorganize our workflow and we were able to deliver on time.
Interviewer: That's impressive. Will you be able to implement similar strategies here if needed?
Situation: Doctor's Appointment
Patient: After the surgery, will I be able to play sports again?

Doctor: Most patients are able to return to moderate physical activity within three months. You should be able to play non-contact sports by then, but you won't be able to participate in high-impact activities for at least six months.
Patient: I understand. I'm glad I'll be able to stay active in some way during recovery.
Situation: Language Learning
Student: I've been studying English for years, but I haven't been able to become fluent.
Teacher: Fluency takes time. Have you been able to practice with native speakers?
Student: Not regularly. I would be able to practice more if I had more opportunities for conversation.
Common Errors and Formal Variations:
"I am able speak French." ❌ → "I am able to speak French." ✓ (missing "to")
"She will can swim after lessons." ❌ → "She will be able to swim after lessons." ✓ (incorrect future with "can")
"They have could finish the project." ❌ → "They have been able to finish the project." ✓ (incorrect perfect with "could")
"We are able swimming." ❌ → "We are able to swim." ✓ (incorrect verb form after "able to")
"I am able to assist you with this matter." (formal) vs. "I can help you with this." (informal)
"The candidate should be able to demonstrate proficiency in data analysis." (formal) vs. "The candidate should know how to analyze data." (informal)
"We were not able to accommodate your request." (formal) vs. "We couldn't do what you asked." (informal)
📖 Reading Practice
Adapting to Remote Work

When the global pandemic forced companies to shift to remote work in early 2020, many organizations and employees weren't able to adapt immediately. The transition presented numerous challenges that businesses had to overcome quickly.

"Initially, we weren't able to maintain our usual productivity levels," explains Maria Santos, HR Director at TechGlobal. "Many employees hadn't been able to set up proper home offices, and our IT infrastructure wasn't able to support the sudden increase in remote connections."

However, with time and investment, most companies have been able to adjust to the new reality. "After implementing new collaboration tools, we've been able to improve communication significantly," Santos continues. "Our teams are now able to coordinate effectively despite being physically separated."

The experience has transformed how businesses view remote work. "We've been able to recognize the benefits of flexible arrangements," says Carlos Mendes, CEO of DigitalSolutions. "By next year, we will have been able to redesign our entire workflow to support a hybrid model. Employees will be able to choose whether to work from home or come to the office on most days."

For many workers, developing new skills has been crucial. "I wasn't able to manage my time effectively at first," admits Ana Ferreira, a marketing specialist. "But I've been able to establish a routine that works for me. I'm now even able to achieve better work-life balance than before the pandemic."
Questions:
What challenges did companies face when transitioning to remote work?
How have companies and employees been able to adapt over time?
Identify five different forms of "be able to" used in the text and explain the time frame each one refers to.
✏️ Practice Exercises
📘 Practice 1 - Form Identification and Transformation
Identify the form of "be able to" in each sentence, then transform it as indicated in parentheses:
She is able to speak three languages fluently. (future simple)
They were able to solve the problem yesterday. (present perfect)
I will be able to attend the conference next month. (past simple)
We have been able to increase sales by 20%. (past perfect)
He might be able to help you with your project. (negative form)
The company has been able to expand into new markets. (future perfect)
They are not able to meet the deadline. (conditional with "would")
I was able to finish the report before the meeting. (future with "should")
📘 Practice 2 - Sentence Completion
Choose the most appropriate form to complete each sentence:
After completing the advanced course, I _______ speak almost like a native. a. can b. will be able to c. am able d. could
Despite the difficult circumstances, they _______ finish the project on time last month. a. could b. were able to c. can d. are able to
She _______ play the piano since she was a child. a. has been able to b. is able to c. will be able to d. was able to
If I had more time, I _______ help you with your homework. a. can b. am able to c. would be able to d. could be able to
By the end of next year, we _______ pay off all our debts. a. will be able to b. will have been able to c. are able to d. can
I tried several times but _______ convince him to change his mind. a. wasn't able to b. haven't been able to c. wouldn't be able to d. can't
📘 Practice 3 - Error Correction
Identify and correct the errors related to "be able to" in these sentences:
After the course, I will can speak better English.
She has could solve difficult problems since she was young.
They are able finish the project by Friday.
We not able to attend the meeting yesterday.
He will been able to drive after he gets his license.
I am able swimming since I was a child.
They would able to help if they had more time.
She have been able to improve her skills significantly.
📘 Practice 4 - Translation Challenge
Translate these Portuguese sentences into English, paying special attention to the correct form of "be able to":
Depois do treinamento, eu serei capaz de usar o novo software.
Ela tem sido capaz de manter uma rotina de exercícios há seis meses.
Eles não foram capazes de resolver o problema ontem.
Você será capaz de comparecer à reunião amanhã?
Nós nunca fomos capazes de entender por que ele tomou aquela decisão.
Até o final do ano, teremos sido capazes de implementar todas as mudanças.
Eu seria capaz de ajudar se tivesse mais informações.
Ela não tem sido capaz de dormir bem ultimamente.
🔁 Deep Review
"Be able to" is a versatile structure that provides greater flexibility than modal verbs for expressing ability. Here's a summary of key points:
"Be able to" can be used in all tenses, aspects, and with other modal verbs, unlike "can/could"
It's formed with the appropriate form of "be" + "able to" + base verb
In the past tense, "was/were able to" often emphasizes successful completion of a specific action
"Will be able to" is essential for discussing future abilities since "can" has no future form
"Have/has/had been able to" expresses ability over a period of time
"Be able to" is often preferred in formal or professional contexts
"Would be able to" is used for hypothetical or conditional abilities
Common errors include omitting "to," using "can" with future forms, and incorrect verb forms after "able to"
Quick Review Questions:
When would you use "was able to" instead of "could"?
How do you express ability in the future perfect tense?
What's the difference between "I can't speak Japanese" and "I haven't been able to speak Japanese"?
How would you express a hypothetical ability using "be able to"?
🏠 Homework
📅 Day 1 - Writing

Write a personal statement (250-300 words) for a job application or university admission, focusing on your abilities and achievements. Use at least six different forms of "be able to" (different tenses, with modals, etc.). Underline each instance and identify its form in parentheses.
📅 Day 2 - Listening
Watch this TED Talk: "The power of believing that you can improve" by Carol Dweck (
https://www.ted.com/talks/carol_dweck_the_power_of_believing_that_you_can_improve

). Make notes of five instances where the speaker discusses abilities (either using "be able to," "can/could," or other expressions). For each one, rewrite the statement using a different form of "be able to" that maintains the same meaning.
📅 Day 3 - Grammar
Complete these sentences using the appropriate form of "be able to":
After I finish this course, I _______ apply for better positions.
Despite the difficulties, she _______ complete the marathon last year.
They _______ solve the problem yet, but they're still working on it.
By the time I retire, I _______ save enough for a comfortable lifestyle.
If I had studied harder, I _______ pass the exam.
She _______ play the piano since she was five years old.
We _______ contact him since he changed his phone number.
The company _______ increase profits significantly next quarter if the new product launches successfully.
📅 Day 4 - Speaking
Record yourself answering these questions, using complete sentences with appropriate forms of "be able to":
What skills have you been able to develop in the past few years?
What will you be able to do after you complete your English course?
Describe a situation where you were able to solve a difficult problem.
What would you be able to achieve if you had more free time?
What haven't you been able to accomplish yet that you hope to in the future? Listen to your recording and note any errors in your use of "be able to."
📅 Day 5 - Vocabulary/Context
Create a dialogue between a career counselor and a client discussing future career possibilities. The dialogue should be 12-15 exchanges long and include at least:
2 uses of "will be able to"
2 uses of "would be able to"
1 use of "have been able to"
1 use of "was/were able to"
1 use with another modal verb (might/should/must be able to)
1 negative form of "be able to"
📅 Day 6 - Creativity/Reflection
Choose one option:
Write a short story (250-300 words) about a character who develops a new skill or ability. Use various forms of "be able to" to show the character's progress over time.

Write a reflection (250-300 words) comparing how ability is expressed in English versus Portuguese. Discuss how the flexibility of "be able to" compared to "can/could" affects your expression in English, and include specific examples of situations where the languages differ in how they express ability.
